title.value: Popular and Scientific Discourse on Autism: Representational Cross-Cultural Analysis of Epistemic Communities to Inform Policy and Practice
title.justification: This is clearly indicated as the title of the paper in the provided text.
title.quote: Popular and Scientific Discourse on Autism: Representational Cross-Cultural Analysis of Epistemic Communities to Inform Policy and Practice

extractions.description: The paper explores the trends in health information about autism spectrum disorder (ASD) within popular and scientific communities, analyzing big data from Twitter and PubMed to compare lay and scientific discourse on ASD. It identifies divergences in focus between public perceptions and scientific research, highlighting the implications for policy and practice.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on autism spectrum disorder and the representation of this condition in popular and scientific discourse. It does not explicitly address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: This study explores the trends in health information about autism spectrum disorder within popular and scientific communities.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not address any climate or ecological sustainable development themes. It is centered on social media and scientific discourse on autism.
primary_category.quote: This study explores the trends in health information about autism spectrum disorder within popular and scientific communities.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary climate or ecological sustainable development themes present in this paper. It strictly focuses on autism spectrum disorder and related discourse.
secondary_categories.quote: The results suggest a clear distinction between the focus of topics used in the social media and that of scientific communities.

primary_sub_category.quote: This study provides the first systematic and rigorous comparison between 2 corpora of interests, in terms of lay representations and scientific research, regarding the significant increase in information available on autism spectrum disorder.

applications.value: Informing policy and practice for autism spectrum disorder
applications.justification: The study aims to inform policymakers about health and social needs of individuals with ASD and to better align research priorities with personal concerns, although it does not relate to ecological aspects.
applications.quote: Finally, our study can inform policy makers on the health and social needs and concerns of individuals with autism and their caregivers.

new_primary_category.quote: This study is the first to analyze lay representations of autism and compare them with those of the scientific community.

new_primary_sub_category.quote: The paper illustrates the potential to use social media as a proxy for the representations of ASD in the society today.
